name: Baker Hughes Company
shift: Energy security (gas, LNG) and power demand
role_in_chain: Gas turbines, compressors and LNG trains (IET) for LNG developers, pipelines and data-center power; oilfield services
om_now: 0.10 (FY2025 pre-tax margin; FY2024 GAAP operating margin 11.1%)
pe_med_10y: n/m (losses or near-zero earnings in most of 2016-2022)
margin_capture_note: Captures more each year: margin from a ~4-5% median to ~10-11%; gas-technology equipment is capacity-constrained; Q3 GAAP net income fell 33% on $214M of adjustments while adjusted EBITDA rose 14%
one_line_note: One order book fed by LNG, data-center power and pipelines, still priced like an oil-services company at 18x after +49% in 3 years

name: Hubbell Incorporated
role_in_chain: Utility T&D components (connectors, arresters, substation gear) plus data-center electrical products
backlog_growth_yoy: not disclosed (Q3 2026 release: orders strong, continued backlog build)
margin_capture_note: Captures: operating margin 20.7% FY2025 vs 14.1% ten-year median, held at 21.8% in Q3 2026 while revenue rose 25%; sells to hundreds of utilities so no single buyer sets price
one_line_note: The least crowded way to own utility capex and data-center electrical demand at once; weakness is that it gives no backlog number, so visibility rests on its words

name: TransDigm Group Incorporated
role_in_chain: Sole-source engineered aircraft components sold to primes, DoD and airlines (OEM and aftermarket)
margin_capture_note: Captures the most in the chain: operating margin 45.6% FY2026 vs 42.9% median; sole-source parts let it price above cost, which also draws DoD pricing scrutiny
one_line_note: Where the defense margin actually lands, priced at its own history after only a 38% three-year gain; half its business is commercial aftermarket, so this is not a pure defense bet

name: EMCOR Group, Inc.
role_in_chain: Electrical and mechanical construction and services for data centers, fabs, hospitals, factories
margin_capture_note: Captures via labor scarcity: operating margin 10.1% in 2025 vs 5.1% median (2.9% in 2020); at median margin the P/E would be about 44x, so margin durability is the bet
one_line_note: Real backlog growth across many end markets at only 15% above its own P/E history; the risk is margin reversion, not demand

name: Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc.
role_in_chain: Only builder of US aircraft carriers, co-builder of nuclear submarines, amphibious ships
margin_capture_note: Weak but turning: 5.3% in 2025 vs 7.5% median; Q3 2026 7.0% vs 5.0%; the Navy holds pricing, the bottleneck is HII labor
one_line_note: Backlog up 55% on submarine awards with margins recovering from a trough; only +28% in 3 years, 36% below its 52-week high

name: General Dynamics Corporation
role_in_chain: Submarines (Electric Boat), combat vehicles, munitions, IT; plus Gulfstream jets
backlog_growth_yoy: +87% vs $118.0B at Dec 2025 (XBRL); +61% vs prior quarter
margin_capture_note: Flat: 10.2% in 2025 vs 10.9% median; Marine margin +80 bps in Q3; Gulfstream book-to-bill 1.4x adds a commercial leg
one_line_note: Backlog jumped $84B in one quarter on submarine awards; margins do not move, so earnings grow with volume only

name: Dycom Industries, Inc.
role_in_chain: Fiber, long-haul and data-center connectivity construction for carriers and hyperscalers
om_now: 0.066 (pre-tax margin FY ended Jan-2026; no operating-income tag)
margin_capture_note: Weak: organic Communications adjusted EBITDA margin 13.6% vs 14.9% in Q2 FY27; customers are a few large carriers, so price is negotiated, not set
one_line_note: Record backlog at its own historical multiple and 58% off its high after a guidance miss; cheap for a margin reason worth checking next quarter

name: Trane Technologies plc
role_in_chain: Chillers and thermal management for data centers and commercial buildings
margin_capture_note: Captured over 10 years (11.9% in 2016 to 18.6% in 2025) but flat lately: Q3 2026 GAAP margin 19.9% vs 20.3%
one_line_note: Backlog up 73% and organic bookings +20%, at 26% above its own P/E history; margins have stopped rising, which caps the upside

name: Eaton Corporation plc
role_in_chain: Switchgear, UPS, power distribution for data centers, utilities and factories
margin_capture_note: Captures some: margin ~19% (FY2025 pre-tax plus interest over revenue) vs ~16-17% history; book-to-bill 1.3 in Electrical Americas
one_line_note: Real backlog growth and pricing, but it is the obvious electrical name and trades 21% above its own P/E history

name: Cheniere Energy, Inc.
shift: Energy security (gas, LNG) and power demand
role_in_chain: Largest US LNG exporter: liquefaction under long-term fixed-fee SPAs plus marketing
backlog_or_rpo_latest_usd_bn: not verified (RPO last tagged in XBRL at 2019: 108.8)
backlog_growth_yoy: not verified (new SPAs with QatarEnergy up to 4 mtpa, Oct 2026; SPL expansion FID)
margin_capture_note: Fixed liquefaction fees are protected; the marketing margin is exposed to the 2026-2028 LNG supply wave (Q3 2026 operating margin 31% vs 41%)
one_line_note: Cheapest name here against its own history, with new long-term contracts and raised guidance; cheap because the market expects an LNG glut

name: Northrop Grumman Corporation
role_in_chain: B-21 bomber, Sentinel ICBM, space systems, solid rocket motors, munitions
margin_capture_note: None: margin 10.8% vs 11.4% median; fixed-price B-21 LRIP lots carry losses (a $226M unfavorable EAC in Q1 2025)
one_line_note: Least crowded prime with real backlog growth, but it is a volume story with no pricing power

name: RTX Corporation
role_in_chain: Missiles and air defense (Raytheon), engines and aftermarket (Pratt & Whitney), avionics (Collins)
margin_capture_note: Some: Q3 2026 margin 13.4% vs 11.2%; engine aftermarket and missile scarcity give it more pricing than other primes
one_line_note: The missile bottleneck with a $340B book, but up 163% and at 1.5x its own P/E history

name: Kinder Morgan, Inc.
shift: Energy security (gas, LNG) and power demand
role_in_chain: Largest US gas pipeline network: feedgas to LNG terminals and gas to new power plants
margin_capture_note: Regulated and contracted tariffs: margin stable at 28% vs 27%; volume, not price
one_line_note: Record gas expansion backlog, but up 112% in 3 years and 32% above its own P/E history

name: Cummins Inc.
role_in_chain: Backup and prime-power gensets and battery storage for data centers (Power Systems); truck engines
margin_capture_note: Power Systems is lifting the group: Q3 2026 operating margin 15.3% vs 10.2%; truck engines (most of revenue) are weak, which hides the power business
one_line_note: A genset supplier priced as a truck-engine company that has already re-rated 43% above its P/E history; RPO number is ten months old

name: Jacobs Solutions Inc.
role_in_chain: Design and program management for water, data centers, advanced manufacturing, transport
margin_capture_note: Improving: margin 7.2% in 2025 vs 4.4% median; but adjusted net revenue only +8% vs gross +34%, so much of the growth is pass-through and acquisition
one_line_note: Backlog +27% at its own EV/EBIT history; underlying growth is single digits, so this is a steady designer, not a tide rider

name: Equinix, Inc.
role_in_chain: Data-center shells, power and interconnection landlord (retail colocation)
margin_capture_note: Moderate: capacity-constrained space and interconnection lets it raise prices; operating margin 23.3% in Q3 2026 vs 20.5% a year earlier; REIT P/E is inflated by depreciation, so compare only to its own history
one_line_note: The landlord leg of the AI build, priced at its own history after a 41% three-year gain; revenue only +11% so it is a steady toll, not a rocket

name: L3Harris Technologies, Inc.
role_in_chain: Solid rocket motors (Aerojet), sensors, space, tactical radios
margin_capture_note: Recovering: 9.0% in 2024 vs 11.9% median, Q3 2026 13.0% vs 11.0%
one_line_note: Owns a real bottleneck (rocket motors) but revenue grows 7% and the multiple is 29% above history

name: BWX Technologies, Inc.
role_in_chain: Sole-source naval nuclear reactors and fuel; commercial nuclear components
margin_capture_note: None: cost-plus Navy work; margin 12.6% in 2025 vs 15.9% median
one_line_note: A monopoly that cannot raise prices, at 1.5x its own P/E; 50% below its 52-week high after the nuclear trade cooled

name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
role_in_chain: F-35, PAC-3 interceptors, missiles, space
margin_capture_note: Negative: margin 10.3% in 2025 vs 12.9% median after program charges; Q3 2026 11.8% vs 12.3%
one_line_note: Largest backlog jump among primes, but margins are below history and the P/E is 1.8x its median on depressed earnings

name: Granite Construction Incorporated
role_in_chain: Heavy civil: highways, bridges, site work, aggregates, federal and mission-critical sites
margin_capture_note: Improving from a low base: 6.4% in 2025 vs 2.2% median, Q3 2026 12.7% vs 10.0%; public-works bidding limits pricing power
one_line_note: Below its own multiple history with record committed work, but tied to the next federal highway bill more than to any private shift

name: Caterpillar Inc.
role_in_chain: Gensets, recip engines and Solar gas turbines for behind-the-meter data-center power; construction and mining equipment
margin_capture_note: Some: Q3 2026 operating margin 20.4% vs 17.3%
one_line_note: RPO more than doubled, but at 1.8x its own P/E history the power story is largely in the price

name: nVent Electric plc
role_in_chain: Enclosures, liquid-cooling and electrical connection products for data centers and utilities
backlog_growth_yoy: not verified (no prior-year RPO figure found)
margin_capture_note: Some: Q3 2026 operating margin 18.6% vs 15.8% on organic sales +44%
one_line_note: Growth is real (record sales and orders) but the multiple is already 42% above its own history

name: Carpenter Technology Corporation
role_in_chain: Specialty alloys for jet engines, defense, power-generation turbines
backlog_growth_yoy: not disclosed (Q1 FY27 release: bookings rising)
margin_capture_note: Captures heavily: operating margin 22.5% vs 7.8% median; alloys segment 37.7% adjusted margin on pricing actions; at median margin the P/E would be about 70x
one_line_note: Pricing power is proven, but the stock is up 304% and only looks cheap against history because margins tripled; 56% off its 52-week high

name: Powell Industries, Inc.
role_in_chain: Custom medium-voltage switchgear and power control rooms for utilities, LNG, data centers
margin_capture_note: Captures more than anyone in the chain: 21% operating margin vs 2.9% ten-year median; at median margin the P/E would be well over 100x
one_line_note: Best pricing evidence in the grid chain but up 456% in 3 years; the multiple looks normal only because margins are seven times their history
